assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only silent-witch:louis-miller@light-novel#v1-character-monograph (the canonical V1 character monograph SW_CHARACTER_LOUIS_MILLER.md, version 1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese light novels V01-V12 with the companions IV -after- (AFTER04) and IX -extra- (EXTRA09) and the two -another- prequel volumes, as closed at snapshot 60b21a7 (sixteen units). Louis is seen mostly from outside in the numbered track, through short strategic secret episodes, and from inside in the prequels, which were admitted and read last; the monograph marks prequel evidence as retrospective and does not use it to revise a frozen numbered reading. Paratext is cited only as paratext. The monograph was written by a fresh-context analyst from name-filtered retrieval (V05-V08 and V10 read only in part) and checked mechanically and for knowledge boundaries by the integrator; neither reread the Japanese source, and owner semantic acceptance is not claimed. The master ledger, the readings, the relationship arguments, the project's reconstruction-readiness assessment and the Codex G2 material are not curated on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. No web serial, adaptation or translation is used, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Evidence runs from Louis's childhood in the Dangrots brothel through Minerva, the Magic Corps, the Sage selection and his marriage (all before V01, from the prequels, retrospective), the AFTER04 prologue and the first EXTRA09 chapter (his first year or so as a Sage, also before V01), and the numbered track to the end of V12. Facts disclosed late (Vivian's request, Clockford's suppression of his candidacy) belong to the world at every earlier state, but Louis's knowledge follows the monograph: he never learns that Adolf started the rumour about Birdland, and he learns of the suppression only when told. Within V01-V12 his state changes little and his roles accumulate; the assessed split is the V09 council (V09 obs. 072, 104, 137), before which he assumes Monica will never ask for help and after which he dates his third method, connections, to that defeat (V11 obs. 183). The V11 fog regression (obs. 119-149) is a bounded episode, not a state. No state after V12 is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: Three located mechanisms explain his choices. He is quick to see malice and blind to goodwill (Rutherford's judgment, ANOTHER-UPPER obs. 183); his effort always answers a slight (section 5.1); and he describes his acts in the language of interest while his conduct shows attachment (section 5.4, tested on Monica, Lionel and Rosalie). Together they predict his mistakes, not only his competence: the wrong verdict on Monica (V03 obs. 130-131) that V09 defeats (obs. 072), the sarcasm about the engagement that Rosalie overhears and believes (ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 066, 122), and his blindness to Adolf's longing (V11 obs. 143, 170). Section 6.4 explains why the Monica model failed: it was a model of his own younger self. Not A: one literary monograph from filtered retrieval, no source reread, and where serious harm to Monica conflicts with a mission or political aim the evidence divides (section 6.2). Not C: what decides most choices is stated. Family and the vulnerable come first (V10 obs. 177; V11 obs. 014; ANOTHER-UPPER obs. 115-117; ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 157). Mission and political ends govern how he uses Monica and Glen. Her standing and self-respect govern what he spends on her (V04 obs. 096; ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 159).

The prequels give six ordered states with mechanisms (section 3.2: boy without ambition, delinquent, student defeated into theory, friend who learns he is blind to goodwill, lover, graduate vowing to become a Sage), and the lower volume continues them through Corps head, Sage, husband (section 4). Each transition names its cause (sections 4.1-4.5). The numbered track adds the V09 defeat and the V11 change of method. Not A: within V01-V12 the monograph finds roles accumulating rather than states changing, the prequel states are retrospective and were read last, and no finer chronology than the readings' ages is computed (section 14).

Register is described with its switching conditions. Formal first person, the colleague-of-the-same-intake address and elaborate, slightly archaic polite endings thin to bare imperatives under pressure (V01 reading section 6.13; SW-S-0016). He has a mock-scriptural motto. He breaks into rough speech when attacked (V09 obs. 048, 055) and into the sealed northern accent under the V11 fog (obs. 119-124) and with Rosalie in the carriage (ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 147-151). The prequel explains the polish as a sealed accent learned for Birdland's terms (ANOTHER-UPPER obs. 211-212). Not B: the monograph deliberately quotes no Japanese, never names the pronoun or endings, and gives few full lines, so wording is weakly constrained; there is no voice or delivery evidence (section 8.1).

Recurring habits are located, and each has a cause. Jam goes in coffee, tea and on his wife's cooking, and is his universal gift (section 10.1). He drinks liquor because he does not trust taps (section 10.2). He keeps the twelve coins unspent, and wears gloves and long hair as signs of wealth (section 7.2). He mends, cooks and tends hair (V11 obs. 094; ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 081). He hates shovelling snow, and pads an injury report to take his family to a hot spring (V11 obs. 213). Not B: his family life and daily routine as a Sage are short scenes (section 2.4), and most of this material is comic tics rather than a routine.

Section 9 tabulates consistent conduct toward ten recipients, and its prose argues the main cases. Monica: coercion with investment, a wrong model, respect after defeat. Rosalie: devotion, concealment by sarcasm and polish, voice restored. Rutherford: defiance and dependence. Majer: unreserved respect. Owen: protection, trust and gruff teasing. Lionel: friendship hidden behind faction talk. Glen: use, harsh teaching and private, proportionate punishment. Lynn: mutual benefit with stated terms, including allowing her destruction (V07 obs. 004). Adolf: wounding indifference and vengeance for others. Restraint depends on who is watching: Birdland in the selection and at V12 (ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 106; V12 obs. 181). Not A: Carla, Lynn and Birdland are thin, and the Glen and Monica dyads were retrieved only partly from V05-V08 and V10.

Interior access comes from two complementary sources. The prequels' continuous narration covers what he wants and fears, including the adult Corps head and Sage of the lower volume (ANOTHER-UPPER obs. 030, 080, 097, 183-184, 202; ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 018, 091). The numbered track's secret episodes show what he calculates (V01 obs. 116-119; V03 obs. 128-131; V08 obs. 185-188). Not A: in V01-V12 his motive rests on short strategic episodes and inference from conduct (section 14), and the inside view arrived last.

Combat and conflict are specified with their causes. He answers slights out of proportion (ANOTHER-UPPER obs. 046, 083, 159). He turns rules into loopholes and barriers into weapons: barrier fist, ramming, Mirror Prison, tripping and choking inside the duel barrier (section 4.2; V09 obs. 063-065). He investigates by controlling information and studying a friend's habits (ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 083-085, 137). His violence is a learned way to make a place safe, and he renounces it when it would cost him something he wants (sections 7.3, 9.10). V09 shows that he can be waylaid and outfought (obs. 048-072). Not A: his maiming of Adolf and other serious violence is uncondemned and largely comic, so its limits are not tested (section 13.4).

His positions are located but his deliberation is not. Testing a pupil is a teacher's duty (V02 obs. 010). Whatever suits the powerful becomes the truth (V08 obs. 252). He would publish everything, at the cost of Isaac's execution, by Monica's judgment (V08 obs. 253; V09 obs. 049). He proposes sealing witnesses' memories (V07 obs. 138). He coerces with threats he privately discounts (V01 obs. 118). He takes vengeance for others, not himself (ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 140). The books neither condemn nor endorse his violence (section 13.4). Not B: no reasoning chain on a moral conflict is shown from inside. Not D: the stances are explicit and recur across units.

His own play has several modes, and the monograph explains what they do. He lies outrageously and deadpan (that the Silent Witch kills at a glance, V05 obs. 045; the passing woodcutter, V07 obs. 019). He makes theatrical threats (to bury Rutherford, V04 obs. 040), uses a mock-scriptural motto, and fends off Lynn with an hour of praise for his wife (EXTRA09 obs. 093). His sarcasm conceals attachment, and it fails when a listener takes it literally (ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 066, 122). The comedy of his coercion is separated by whether harm to the target is registered (section 10.3). Not A: the humour is seen through a narrator's comic framing more often than through his own view.

The monograph covers all sixteen closed units, with 594 checked observation references and declared limits. It is one literary monograph from name-filtered retrieval in which V05-V08 and V10 were read only in part (known defect 1). Neither analyst nor integrator reread the source (defect 5), and owner semantic acceptance is not claimed. Two cross-unit inferences are labelled as such (defect 3). Not B: the retrieval gap falls in the mission years, where the Monica and Glen dyads are most active.

The evidence affirmatively shows what he gets wrong and where he fails. His verdict on Monica is contradicted on the page and defeated at V09 (SW-F-0021; V09 obs. 072, 137). He never reads Adolf's longing, and that blindness costs Rosalie a fall and Owen a poisoning (section 9.8). His refinement estranges Rosalie (ANOTHER-LOWER obs. 056-059). He allows Lynn's destruction (V07 obs. 004). Section 13 tests four counterreadings against evidence. Section 11 records seams it leaves unresolved: the house against the contract stone, and the timing of the previous selection. Not A: the monograph itself warns that filtered retrieval may have missed observations.

The monograph sets out three orders: source and reading, diegetic, and revelation (section 1). It keeps prequel evidence retrospective, and it marks what Louis knows apart from what the reader knows: Adolf's rumour, Vivian's request, Clockford's suppression (sections 4.1, 4.4, 5.2). Stages are located by unit and observation. Not A: ages are approximate, the previous selection's timing is reconciled only by inference, and no finer chronology is computed (sections 11, 14).

conditions: Output is illustrative and labelled noncanonical, never presented as a quotation.
Output is in English or another rendering that describes register; no Japanese pronoun, ending or lexical claim is made.

The register is chosen by the documented conditions: polished politeness by default, hardening to command under pressure, rough speech when attacked or provoked about his looks, the northern accent only when the polish drops (the fog regression, or private sincerity with Rosalie).
The recipient is one of the sampled recipients, at a named state, chosen before wording.
scenario_readiness.note: The switching conditions for his registers constrain an illustrative rendering. The lexical items do not, because the monograph quotes none.

conditions: A Sage-duty, dragon-subjugation, investigation or court-politics problem in which he protects family and the vulnerable first, uses capable juniors instrumentally, and invests in the standing of people he respects.
Novel provocation by a rival or a slight, answered with effort or disproportionate force unless someone whose approval he wants is watching.
Pre-V09 he assumes Monica will not ask for help; post-V09 he credits connections as method.

Abstain where the scenario requires choosing between serious harm to Monica and a mission or political aim, or depends on the post-V12 Kerbeck dragon mission, the seventh Sage, Carla's family matter or whom Lynn loves.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Adult Sage between the AFTER04 prologue and the end of V12, with the state named as before or after the V09 council; prequel states only as retrospective history.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Monica, Rosalie, Glen, Owen, Lynn, Rutherford, Lionel, Adolf or Birdland as sampled; a stranger gets the polished register without invented history.
setting_constraints: Settings the evidence samples: Sage duty, Magic Corps work, missions, court and family home.
No post-V12 events and no reliance on withheld identities.
Serious violence is predicted only in the forms the evidence locates.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded transfer is supported where the three mechanisms and the recipient table decide; abstain where the choice turns on the pride-against-care conflict over serious harm to Monica, or on an open thread.

conditions: Meals, drink, gifts, travel, errands or household care with Rosalie, Owen, Glen, Monica or Lynn.
Jam, liquor and money habits as located; tending and mending are skills from the brothel.
Affection to friends in gruff or commanding register, not stated warmth.
scenario_readiness.note: Recurring habits and recipient-specific gruffness are located; daily routine as a Sage is thin.

conditions: Predict his stance on the located questions: exposing frauds and Clockford's faction, testing pupils, coercing capable colleagues, vengeance on behalf of others.
State the stance and its stated rationale, not an invented deliberation.
Abstain on novel moral dilemmas outside these positions.
scenario_readiness.note: Only located positions are supported; no inner moral reasoning is shown.

conditions: The partner is Rosalie at a named state: Minerva courtship, the polished engagement and its misreading, the carriage restoration, or marriage.
Devotion concealed by sarcasm or polish in public, sincerity in the northern accent in private.
No other romance; Lynn's and Glen's feelings are theirs, not his.
scenario_readiness.note: Rosalie is the only sampled romance, across school courtship, the polished engagement and marriage.

conditions: Sage or Corps duty, dragon subjugation, investigation through information control, teaching Glen, or coordinating his connections (V11 obs. 182-188).
Barrier-based tactics as located, including rule loopholes.
No unshown Sage deliberation and no Spirit-King summoning detail.
scenario_readiness.note: His professional method is the best-located domain after relationships.

known_limits.statement: The monograph was written by a fresh-context analyst from a read-only copy of the readings, and neither analyst nor integrator reread the Japanese source; no Japanese is quoted. Owner semantic acceptance is not claimed.
Numbered-track evidence was gathered through section reads and name-filtered observation rows; V05-V08 and V10 were read only in part, so observations of Louis in the mission years may be missing.
In V01-V12 his interior appears only in short, mostly strategic secret episodes; motive there rests on inference from conduct, and the continuous inside view comes from the prequels, read last.
Prequel evidence is marked retrospective: it explains the numbered track and does not revise a frozen numbered reading.

Where serious harm to Monica conflicts with a mission or political aim the evidence divides (V07 obs. 136-138; V08 obs. 188, 253 against V04 obs. 096; V02 obs. 096). The monograph treats pride and care as fused and does not adjudicate which decides.
Accent, register and address rest on written prose; nothing about voice or delivery is claimed.
Open at V12 and unpredicted: the Kerbeck black-dragon mission, how he learned Spirit-King summoning, Carla's family matter, the selection of the seventh Sage and whom Lynn loves.

Two points are labelled inference: that Louis was the unnamed past abuser behind the duel barrier's rule, and that his V11 'connections' self-report describes method learned rather than connections first acquired.
V10's remark that Lynn's contract stone cost him his dream of a house is unreconciled with the prequel's purchase of a house after the contract.

Withheld identities (the patron called by the honorific, the seventh Sage, the executed researcher, the pale-gold girl) are not named, and his soirée suspicion of the second prince is his perception, not knowledge.
No probe, held-out test or validation of predictions about Louis exists in the cited evidence.
